title: What The Bass Guitar Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal music philosophy absurdist groove
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The bass guitar is the instrument nobody notices is there
Until it isn't — and then the whole song seems to disappear
Into a collection of sounds that don't add up to a room
The bass guitar holds the bottom and the bottom holds the boom

[Pre-Chorus]
Every great song you've loved has a bass line in it somewhere
That you didn't consciously register — it was just there

[Chorus]
What does the bass guitar know that I don't know?
It knows the bottom of the song is what keeps the top in flow
What does the bass guitar know from the back of the stage?
It knows that holding things together is the most underpaid wage
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The bass player and the drummer look at each other differently
Than anyone else in the band — they have their own treaty
Between the kick drum and the root note there's a conversation
That the audience receives as groove without further explanation

[Bridge]
I've been the bass of various ensembles over the years
Not literally — I play nothing well — but in the role that keeps the gears
Turning without being the one who takes the bow at the end
The bass guitar is what I aspire to in the part I tend

[Outro]
Bass guitar knows… the bottom holds the top… bass guitar knows
That's my boy
